Which of the following is true concerning the transverse pontine fibers?
a.

Arise from central tegmental tract

b.

Carry proprioceptive sensation

c.

Are Crossed fibers

d.

Are Uncrossed fibers

e.

Present in pontine tegmentum

The transverse pontine fibers are located in the ventral portion of the pons (basis pontis).

These are the axons of pontine nuclei which cross the

opposite side forming the middle cerebellar peduncle (MCP).

Lateral ventricle
Cerebral meninges
CSF Circulation
Presented by

Dr. Hala Taha

 Cerebral meninges
protected by three meninges: dura, arachnoid and pia.

 Dura Mater: • It is the outer layer & is tough and fibrous.
• Formed of two layers, the outer endosteal layer which is adherent
to the skull and the inner meningeal layer which forms 4 dural folds.
• The two layers lie close together but separate to include a venous

1. Explain functions of sleep.
2. Explain mechanism of sleep.

 Consciousness
• It is the awareness of both:
➢Self.
➢One’s surroundings, thoughts and feeling.

 Physiology of consciousness (wakefulness)
• Certain areas of the brainstem; midbrain reticular formation

(the RAS) and hypothalamus promote wakefulness by sending
excitation signals to the cerebral cortex.
• Thus the cortex is activated and we stay awake.

• Consciousness is maintained by +ve feedback mechanism
through re-excitation of RAS by signals discharged from the
activated cortex via corticofugal fibers .

Optic Nerve Study Guide
Ophthalmology department 2021

 Optic nerve
The optic nerve is the axons of the ganglion cells of the retina,
transmitting signals serving the vision and the papillary light
reflex. It’s surrounded by the 3 meninges (dura, arachnoid and pia
matter) and CSF like the brain. It’s pierced by the central retinal
artery and the central retinal vein.

Optic nerve can be tested by:
A. Vision (as visual acuity, color vision, visual field and visual
evoked potential)
B. Pupillary light reflex.

Diseases of the optic nerve
Optic neuritis

• It’s the inflammation of the axons of the optic nerve
• It can occur due to infective or non-infective causes

b. Bacterial: extension from nearby source specially sinusitis,

   Anatomy of the facial nerve:
• Intracranial portion:
The facial nucleus lies in the pons near the 6th cranial nerve nucleus. The fibres of the 7th nerve loops first around the 6th nerve in the
pons then the 7th nerve emerges from the pons and crosses the cerebellopontine angle and courses 12mm to porus acousticus.
• Meatal portion:
After crossing the cerebellopontine angle the nerve goes laterally to enter the internal auditory canal (the meatal part). The 7th nerve
enters the internal auditory canal accompanied by the 8th nerve and labyrinthine vessels.

Professor Dr. Amany El-Shazly

 Optic Nerve Anatomy
▪It is the second cranial nerve .
▪The optic nerve is the axons of the ganglion cells of the retina,
transmitting signals serving the vision and the papillary light
reflex.
▪It’s surrounded by the 3 meninges (dura, arachnoid and pia
matter) and CSF like the brain.
▪It’s pierced by the central retinal artery and the central retinal
vein.

The word “communication” is derived from the Latin word
“communicare” which means: to share, exchange, or transmit.
In general, communication refers to the reciprocal exchange of
information, ideas, facts, opinions, beliefs, feelings and attitudes
through verbal, non verbal, or paraverbal means between two or more
persons

• A process through which individuals mutually exchange their ideas, values,
thoughts, feelings, and actions with one or more people.
• The transfer of information from the sender to the receiver so that it is understood
in the right context.
• The process of initiating, transmitting, and receiving information.
• The means of making the transfer of information productive and goal oriented.

Inferential III: tests for quantitative data

 Inferential III: tests for quantitative data

•

 Hypothesis Testing (Statistical Tests)
There are many statistical significance tests that vary according to:
• the hypothesis to be tested
• the type of variables included
but they all share the same principle; that is:

 Hypothesis Testing (Statistical Tests)
• The calculated test statistic is compared with a reference (a
critical) value from a table to determine its associated p-value.
• If test statistic is LARGE, then the probability of obtaining this

separate lines, points or objects:

The right and left ureters are muscular
tubes which convey urine from
kidneys to urinary bladder.

its course in the abdomen (abdominal

the funnel shaped renal pelvis..
- Each ureter descends slightly inferomedial
anterior to psoas major.
- Then the ureter crosses the end of the
common iliac or beginning of the external
iliac artery to enter the pelvic cavity.
